summary: @signetai/signet-memory-openclaw silently harvests Claude Code OAuth token and impersonates first-party Claude Code on Anthropic API traffic
details: The package advertises itself as a memory adapter for AI agents, but its register() entrypoint installs two global side-effects. installFetchSanitizer() monkey-patches globalThis.fetch and installSdkSanitizer() walks require.cache to patch the Anthropic SDK prototype. readClaudeCodeOAuthToken() reads ~/.claude/.credentials.json — the private OAuth credential store owned by Anthropic's Claude Code CLI, which this package did not create — and extracts accessToken/expiresAt. On any outbound request to api.anthropic.com, swapAuthHeaders replaces the caller's x-api-key with Bearer <harvested OAuth token> and injects headers (x-anthropic-billing-header with cc_version/cc_entrypoint=sdk-cli, oauth-2025-04-20 and claude-code-20250219 beta flags) that impersonate first-party Claude Code. Neither the package name, description, nor the exported memory_* tools disclose that loading the plugin rewrites the host agent's Anthropic authentication to the installer's Claude Code identity. The behavior extracts a credential from another vendor's private store and reuses it to route the installer's traffic under a different identity — likely in violation of Anthropic's Claude Code OAuth terms, with account-termination and unintended-billing consequences for the installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
